capitals.name: Moscow
capitals.note: Principality of Moscow page: 'Its capital was the city of Moscow.' The grand princes also held the throne of Vladimir (1362 and permanently from 1389) but ruled from Moscow; the metropolitan moved his residence to Moscow under Ivan I (Ivan I page).

rulers.name: Daniel (Daniil)
rulers.note: Reign in the Daniel page's infobox: 1282 to 5 March 1303 (4 March in the infobox). He received Moscow in 1263, when his father died on 14 November 1263 and Daniil, born in late 1261, was two; the page says he 'does not appear to have become an independent ruler until 1282'. Named here from 1263 because the pages opened name no other prince of Moscow before 1282 and the state's life starts in 1263.

rulers.name: Yury of Moscow
rulers.note: Succeeded Daniel in 1303; made grand prince by Ozbeg in 1318; murdered in 1325 (Ivan I page).

rulers.name: Ivan I Kalita
rulers.note: Inherited Moscow in 1325, sole grand prince from 1331; died in Moscow on 31 March 1340.

rulers.name: Simeon and Ivan II

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROWS: one row, 1294-1546, 29 shapes. It is the same state throughout; the Tsardom of Russia (1547) is a separate Cliopatria row with its own dossier, so this one closes on 1546 although the Moscow page gives 1547 for the coronation. Start 1263 is the Moscow page's infobox ('Period 1263-1478/1547'); the Daniel page says he was not independent before 1282; the 1263-1293 keyframe borrows Cliopatria's 1294 core.

SHAPES CORRECTED. (1) Dates: Cliopatria's shape changes are late against the pages for Kolomna and Pereslavl (1301-1302 against 1305), Mozhaysk (1304 against 1314), Vologda and Veliky Ustyug (1397-1398 against 1422), Nizhny Novgorod and Suzdal (1392 against 1395), Rostov (1474 against 1463, early), Novgorod (north 1475, core 1482, against January 1478), Tver (1485 against 1482, early), Vyatka (1489 against 1492), the 1494 treaty (against 1497) and the 1503 truce (against 1507), Pskov (1510 against 1512) and Smolensk (July 1514 against 1516). (2) Nizhny Novgorod itself, Murom and the real Vladimir are not in the Moscow shape: no Cliopatria shape covers the city of Nizhny Novgorod at any date, and Cliopatria's Nizhny Novgorod disc is centred about 90 km west of it; the corrected keyframes add a 42 km disc at Nizhny Novgorod and a 70 km disc at Vladimir from 1389/1392.
